label: final copy step of length-3 sequences
explanation: Fires almost only on the last copy step (t=5, outputting the 3rd original token) of length-3 sequences; there it is active about 89% of the time and holds about 89% of activation mass. Strongest when the input is m (the 2nd original token being fed back), e.g. b m m <DEL> b [m]. Never active in the original or delimiter phases, or at copy steps where the input token is its first occurrence. A weak residual fires on the final or near-final copy step of longer sequences (L=4,6-9), with activations mostly under 0.3 of max; the predicate misses these, which keeps recall at about 0.69.

issues: The claim that it 'never fires at copy steps where the input token appears for the first time' is true but says nothing: every copy-phase input has already appeared earlier in the sequence, so in_first is always 0 there.

The claim 'strongest when the input is m' holds only weakly. (L==3)&(t==5)&(in_tok==m) has precision 1.0, but it covers only 7% of activation mass. The example 'b m m' is a special case where orig(1)==orig(2), and that subset covers just 3% of mass.
The false positives (inputs k, r, g, c reach only about 0.71-0.87 precision) are spread across tokens rather than forming a clean class. Excluding those tokens drops F1 to 0.75.

The missed activations are a real but sparse pattern: firing at the last copy step (to_go==0) of longer sequences, at rates of about 0.1-1.3%. Predicates that add it, such as t==2L-1 or adding L=9,t=17, collapse precision (F1 0.06-0.23). The original predicate stays the best simple one. The 'below 0.3 of max' description of these misses fits what I saw (the largest observed was 0.30).
